label: Bounded and locally finite real times give a minimal identity exercise
meaning: Fix one q3a4 profile, eligible exercise roster, bearer map, relation C and real clock. For each actual identity bearer, take its lower bound and the clock value of a chosen eligible exercise. Indexed local finiteness makes this nonempty compact interval contain finitely many exercise tokens of the bearer. A token achieving the minimum among them has no same-bearer predecessor via any nonempty C-path because strict forwardness along that path would put the predecessor in the same interval with a smaller clock value. The interval argument permits infinitely many later exercises and needs no uniform bound or gap size. A physical application requires independently identifying eligible esse-supply exercises, assigning real clock values to those same tokens, and justifying the quantitative and strict-edge conditions there. Its use to exclude an actual esse-supplier return further requires backward lifting on the same interpretation.
